key_insight: Turbulence closure and inflow uncertainty dominate street-canyon predictions at typical uncertainty levels, while solar forcing can dominate temperature and pollutant variability under weak ventilation when other uncertainties are reduced.
engineering_relevance: Urban exposure studies should constrain turbulence inputs while retaining thermal and vegetation effects near roads and canyon walls.
method: Run RANS simulations of a two-dimensional street canyon under two ventilation regimes.
Train a PCA–MLP surrogate for velocity, temperature, and concentration fields.
Apply global Sobol sensitivity analysis to 24 uncertain inputs while progressively narrowing nonthermal, nonvegetation uncertainties.
evidence_signal: Under weak ventilation, solar forcing dominates temperature variance when other uncertainties are halved and concentration variance when quartered; under strong ventilation, vegetation never overtakes closure constants, even with the dominant constant constrained to ±5%.
watch_item: Thresholds come from a two-dimensional RANS-based surrogate study and may not transfer directly to three-dimensional urban geometries.
paper_title: When does boundary-condition uncertainty outweigh thermal and vegetation effects in street canyon flow? A global sensitivity analysis of input uncertainty
